messages:
ashwin: quick idea — centralize our 'defaults' layer for runtime configs so console + API use the same fallback logic. currently console shows one default, runtime applies another. :confused:

maria: yes please. saw a customer hit a mismatch yesterday where 'quota: soft' in UI but runtime used 'hard' default. we need a single source of truth.

julie: what does "centralize" mean here? single table/service that resolves effective config? or just shared lib?

ashwin: single resolution service (lightweight) — /v1/config/resolve?env=prod&route=foo -> returns effective config + metadata (origin, applied-defaults). keeps resolution deterministic across hosted/dedicated/private.

sam: love the idea but worried about latency. this will be on the hot path for some routes. can we cache per-cohort and return opaque id (config_handle) to avoid resolving every request? :thinking_face:

ashwin: yes — plan: 1) resolve at write/preview time, 2) issue config_handle and TTL, 3) runtime fetches by handle and falls back to local cached copy if service unavailable. fallback policy encoded in resolution response.

maria: fallback policy needs to be explicit. e.g. fallback: { type: "allow_default", priority: [route_override, tenant_default, global_default], circuit_breaker: {max_age_seconds: 300} }

julie: can we show that in console? UX idea: preview modal shows "Effective config" + a small "If resolve service unavailable -> runtime will use: ..." line. ops needs to know what will happen during outage.

ashwin: yes — console will surface two fields: resolved_config (read-only) and resilience_hint (human readable). also add a "simulate outage" checkbox on preview to test fallback.

sam: implementation Q: for Private customers without access to hosted resolve service, do we ship a small resolver binary (golang) that can run in their control plane? or expose a library to embed?

maria: prefer a binary + REST shim. makes upgrades easier and keeps contract surface small. docs should show migration steps and backward compat for older runtime versions.

julie: telemetry — what do we record? I want: resolve_latency_ms, cache_hit, fallback_triggered (bool), fallback_reason (enum), resolver_version. also correlate with config_handle.

ashwin: agreed. also include sample of resolved_vs_runtime_diff when we detect a mismatch at runtime (e.g., route used hard-quota but resolved said soft). that will catch drift.

sam: small nit — config_handle TTL needs to support "pin until replaced" semantics for long-running sessions (we have streaming requests with long-lived state). maybe include an "immutable_until" field or version id that will force reload only on explicit rollouts.

maria: good call. add fields: { version_id, immutable_until_timestamp, recommended_refresh_seconds }. runtime can choose to ignore refresh until session end if immutable_until > now.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: applied patch config-resolver:v0.3.2 to staging (canary 3%). see https://console/redwood/deploys/123 :rocket:

julie: testing checklist for rollout: 1) console preview shows same resolved config as /resolve 2) resolve service handles simulated outage and runtime falls back to cached rules 3) telemetry surfaced in per-route dashboard (cache hit %, fallback count) 4) private packaging tested on air-gapped VM.

ashwin: opt-in rollout plan: start with preview-only (console + /resolve dry-run) for 2 weeks, then enable runtime read of config_handle for non-critical routes (10% traffic), then expand. fallback circuit-breaker defaults to conservative (max_age 60s) during canary.

maria: one API example for docs: ```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
  "https://control-plane.redwood.ai/v1/config/resolve?env=staging&route=quota-check"

# returns JSON: 
# { "config_handle":"cfg_98432ab","resolved":{...},"resilience_hint":"uses tenant_default when resolver offline","ttl":120,"version_id":"v2026-03-18-3" }
```

sam: last question — how do we handle dangerous defaults? e.g., global default for "route_abort_on_error=true" would be risky if applied silently. need explicit audit and an approval flow.

julie: agree — console should mark high-risk defaults and require 1 approver for global-level changes and audit trail. add flag 'safety_locked': true on resolved metadata which prevents auto-promote.

maria: I'll stub the resolver API spec and a draft console wireframe. putting PR up by EOD. :thumbsup:

ashwin: thanks — tagging @sam for packaging and @julie for telemetry dashboards. we'll sync tomorrow at 10am. :calendar:
